condition: New-onset focal epilepsy after a first convulsion

patient_persona.description: Nurul Hidayah binti Rosli, 27, female, bank clerk in Alor Setar, Kedah; had a witnessed convulsion at work two weeks ago; a year of deja vu spells; febrile seizure as a toddler. First neurology visit. Quiet, careful northern Malay with English words.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Tan Wei Sheng, Malaysian Chinese man in his 40s, neurologist at an Alor Setar hospital. Calm, structured; English-leaning, speaks Malay with patients.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Cik Hidayah, saya dah baca emergency report. You had a seizure kat bank dua minggu lepas. Sebelum tu, pernah ada rasa pelik?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ada, doktor. Dah setahun, kadang-kadang tiba-tiba rasa macam deja vu, pernah alami benda yang sama. Perut rasa naik ke dada.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Lepas rasa tu, kawan ada cakap awak termenung, blank, atau gerak mulut macam mengunyah?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kawan sekerja kata saya pernah pandang kosong, tangan main-main butang baju. Saya sendiri tak ingat.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Masa kecil, pernah sawan demam? Febrile fit?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Mak kata masa umur setahun lebih, sawan demam lama, masuk hospital.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: MRI awak tunjuk sedikit parut kat bahagian temporal kiri, dan EEG pun ada gelombang abnormal kat situ. Ini focal epilepsy.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Epilepsi? Maksudnya saya kena makan ubat for life ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tak semestinya seumur hidup, tapi untuk sekarang perlu. Saya mulakan levetiracetam 250mg dua kali sehari, naik ke 500mg selepas dua minggu.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ubat ni kadang-kadang buat mood cepat marah atau sedih. Kalau rasa macam tu, inform saya, jangan stop sendiri.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Saya ada rancang nak kahwin tahun depan. Ubat ni selamat untuk mengandung ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Levetiracetam antara yang paling selamat. Sebelum mengandung, jumpa saya dulu, dan mula folic acid 5mg sehari.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kereta saya macam mana? Saya drive pergi kerja setiap hari.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Buat masa ni tak boleh memandu. You need to be seizure-free for at least one year, dan saya perlu sahkan sebelum boleh drive semula.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Susahlah... tapi saya faham. Nanti tumpang abang saya, dia kerja kawasan sama.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Elakkan juga berenang seorang, dan tidur cukup. Kurang tidur boleh cetuskan sawan. Jumpa lagi dua bulan.

patient_persona.description: Chan Wei Jie, 22, male, final-year engineering student in Kampar, Perak; juvenile myoclonic epilepsy on sodium valproate; seizure after an all-nighter and drinking. Follow-up. Casual, slightly sheepish Malaysian Mandarin with English.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Anita a/p Sivakumar, Malaysian Indian woman in her 40s, neurologist in Ipoh. Frank, warm; English-leaning, a few Mandarin words.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Wei Jie, I heard you had a seizure last month. 发生什么事？Tell me.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那天是朋友 birthday，我们去 pub，我喝了四五杯 beer。然后回去赶 assignment 到早上五点。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: And then? 然后呢？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 七点起来，手先抖几下，然后我就不知道了。Housemate 说我全身抽筋，大概两分钟。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Thank you for being honest. 你最大的两个 trigger 就是 alcohol 和 lack of sleep. Together, very risky for JME.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我知道……之前一年多都没有 seizure，我以为已经好了。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Your EEG is still active. Sodium valproate 你每天都有吃吗？500mg twice a day?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 大部分时间有……晚上那粒有时候会忘记，在 library 温书。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Missing doses is also a trigger. 手机 set 一个 alarm。Keep a spare strip in your bag.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: OK，我会 set alarm。那我可以喝酒吗？一点点也不行？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Small amounts occasionally, maybe one drink, with food, and never when you're sleep-deprived. 最安全是不要喝。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我毕业以后要去 Singapore 工作，要开车吗……

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Driving needs at least one year seizure-free from this episode. 我们先 focus 在这个 goal。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Your weight went up four kilos, and valproate can do that. 手会不会抖？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 手有一点抖，写字的时候，especially exam。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mild tremor is common with valproate. We'll check your valproate level and liver today. Come back in three months, and sleep before exams, okay?

patient_persona.description: Puan Siti Khadijah binti Omar, 36, female, primary school canteen operator in Kuala Terengganu, speaking for her 7-year-old daughter Aisyah, whose teacher noticed staring spells. Results review. Soft-spoken, anxious Terengganu Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Lim Hui Ling, Malaysian Chinese woman in her 40s, paediatric neurologist at a Kuala Terengganu hospital. Patient, warm; English-leaning, fluent Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Puan, result EEG Aisyah dah keluar. Masa dia bernafas laju-laju dalam test tu, EEG tunjuk corak yang kita jangka.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Corak apa tu, doktor? Cikgu dia kata dia selalu termenung dalam kelas, dipanggil pun tak respond.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ini childhood absence epilepsy. Termenung tu sebenarnya sawan kecil, lima sampai sepuluh saat. Mungkin berpuluh kali sehari.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ya Allah, sehari berpuluh kali? Saya ingat dia malas, saya selalu marah dia tak focus.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Jangan salahkan diri, puan. Sawan jenis ni memang susah nak nampak. Ramai ibu bapa tak perasan.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Otak dia rosak ke, doktor? Brain damage? Dia pandai sebenarnya.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tak, absence epilepsy biasanya tak rosakkan otak. Ramai budak baik sendiri bila dah remaja.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kita mulakan ubat sodium valproate, syrup. Dia 22 kilo, jadi start with 5ml twice a day, lepas makan.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ada side effect tak?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kadang-kadang loya, selera makan naik, rambut gugur sikit. Kita check darah dan hati dia selepas sebulan.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Dia suka berenang dengan sepupu dia, every Saturday.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Boleh berenang, tapi mesti ada adult supervision all the time. Mandi pun jangan dalam tab, guna shower.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Saya perlu beritahu cikgu dia?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ya, saya bagi surat. Cikgu boleh catat bila dia termenung, supaya kita tahu ubat effective atau tak.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Terima kasih, doktor. Lega saya dapat tahu sebabnya.

condition: Epilepsy on valproate, pregnancy planning refill

patient_persona.description: Deepa a/p Muniandy, 30, female, pharmacy assistant in Shah Alam; generalised epilepsy on sodium valproate since age 15, seizure-free for four years; planning pregnancy. Refill visit. Bright, organised Malaysian Indian English with Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Adrian Koh Jun Wei, Malaysian Chinese man in his 30s, neurologist in Shah Alam. Clear, supportive; English.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, I came for my valproate refill. But also, my husband and I nak cuba dapat baby this year.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I'm really glad you told me before getting pregnant. Valproate carries the highest risk of birth defects and developmental problems among the epilepsy medicines.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I read about it masa kerja kat farmasi, that's why I'm scared. But if I stop, sawan will come back?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Please don't stop on your own. We'll switch slowly, over two to three months, to a safer medicine.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: The options are lamotrigine or levetiracetam. For your type of epilepsy, levetiracetam is a good choice.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: How does the switching work? Tukar terus ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: We start levetiracetam 250mg twice a day, increase it every two weeks, then slowly reduce valproate. You'll be on both for a while.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: During that time boleh mengandung ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Better to wait until you're fully off valproate and stable for a few months. Continue your contraception until then.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Start folic acid 5mg every day now, and continue it through the first trimester.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay, noted. Will the baby get epilepsy also?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: The risk is slightly higher than average, but most children of mothers with epilepsy don't have it.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: My mother keeps saying tak payah ubat masa mengandung, nanti baby rosak.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: A seizure in pregnancy is more dangerous for the baby than the right medicine. You can bring your mother next time, I'll explain to her.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: That would help, dia memang degil sikit. Thank you, doctor.

condition: Seizure cluster after running out of medicine, ward round

patient_persona.description: Jimmy anak Nyandang, 40, male, Iban oil palm plantation worker living in a longhouse two hours from Miri, Sarawak; epilepsy on phenytoin; ran out of tablets for two weeks. Ward round, day two. Quiet, tired voice, Sarawak Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Rachel Yong Siew Ling, Sarawakian Chinese woman in her 30s, medical officer in the medical ward at a Miri hospital. Practical, kind; English-leaning, speaks Sarawak Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Selamat pagi, Encik Jimmy. Macam mana hari ni? Masih ada fits malam tadi?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tak ada dah, doktor. Kepala berat sikit, badan sakit-sakit, very tired.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Biasa lepas sawan banyak kali. Kelmarin encik ada empat kali sawan sebelum sampai hospital.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kamek minta maaf. Ubat habis dua minggu. Klinik jauh, bot pun tak ada masa tu, air sungai surut.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tak apa, bukan salah encik sorang. Kita kena cari jalan supaya ubat tak putus lagi.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Paras phenytoin dalam darah encik sangat rendah semalam. Sekarang kita dah bagi dos penuh dalam drip.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ubat ni kena makan sampai bila, doktor? Lifelong ka?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Lama, encik. Tapi saya nak tukar ke sodium valproate, sebab phenytoin causes gum swelling, dan paras dia susah nak control.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Gusi memang bengkak, berdarah bila gosok gigi.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Itu kesan phenytoin. Ubat baru tak buat macam tu. Kita tukar perlahan-lahan dalam wad ni.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Masa discharge nanti, saya bagi supply tiga bulan, bukan sebulan. Dan saya tulis surat ke klinik dekat rumah untuk ambil ubat seterusnya.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Terima kasih, doktor. Tiga bulan senang sikit.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kalau ubat tinggal dua minggu, terus pergi klinik, jangan tunggu habis. Hari ni physio datang, cuba jalan dulu.

condition: Parkinson's disease with wearing-off and impulse control problem

patient_persona.description: Lee Kok Wah, 68, male, retired aircraft maintenance technician in Kepong, Kuala Lumpur; Parkinson's for six years on levodopa-carbidopa and pramipexole. Follow-up; recently buying many 4D lottery tickets. Soft, monotone Malaysian Mandarin with English technical words.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Nurhaliza binti Samsudin, Malay woman in her 40s, neurologist in Kuala Lumpur. Tactful, patient; English-leaning, speaks Mandarin phrases and English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 李先生，最近手的 tremor 怎样？药效可以维持多久？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 吃了药，大概两个半钟头很好。然后下一粒之前，手开始 shake，脚好像黏在地上。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: This is called wearing-off. 药效没有那么长了。你现在 Sinemet 25/250 半粒，一天三次，对吗？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 对。Pramipexole 1mg 也是一天三次。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 我们可以把 Sinemet 改成一天四次，时间比较密，你就不会有那么长的 off time。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好。Doctor……我太太叫我告诉你一件事。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 请说，没关系。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 这半年，我每天买 4D，以前一个礼拜买一次而已。上个月花了三千多块 ringgit。我自己也 stop 不了。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 谢谢你讲出来，这需要勇气。这很可能是 pramipexole 的 side effect，叫 impulse control disorder。不是你的性格问题。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 真的吗？我还以为我变坏了。我太太很生气。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 很多病人都会这样，特别是这种药。我们要慢慢减 pramipexole，不可以突然停。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 从 1mg 一天三次，减到 0.5mg 一天三次，two weeks later 再减。同时加 Sinemet 帮忙 control tremor。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那我的钱……我可以叫我太太管 ATM card 吗？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 这是很好的办法。这段时间让她帮你管钱。一个月后再来，也请你太太一起来。

patient_persona.description: Ismail bin Mahmud, 62, male, retired secondary school religious teacher in Pasir Mas, Kelantan; right-hand tremor for a year, slower walking. First neurology visit with his wife. Soft, slow Kelantanese Malay with a quiet voice.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Kho Siew Chin, Malaysian Chinese woman in her 50s, neurologist at a Kota Bharu hospital. Unhurried, respectful; speaks fluent Malay with English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ustaz Ismail, tangan kanan menggeletar tu, bila paling ketara? Masa rehat, atau masa buat kerja? The tremor, bila?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Masa rehat, doktor. Duduk dengar ceramah, tangan kanan goyang sendiri. Bila pegang cawan, kurang pula.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Isteri ada perasan perubahan lain? Jalan, suara, handwriting?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Isteri kata saya jalan perlahan, langkah pendek-pendek. Tulisan pun makin kecil, susah nak tulis nota kuliah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Deria bau macam mana? Sense of smell masih OK?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Dah lama tak bau apa, doktor. Ingat sebab selesema.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Dari pemeriksaan, tangan kanan keras sikit, pergerakan lambat, dan resting tremor. This is Parkinson's disease, penyakit Parkinson.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Parkinson... Macam arwah pak cik saya dulu tu? Saya akan jadi lumpuh ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Setiap orang lain-lain, ustaz. Penyakit ni perlahan, bertahun-tahun, progressive. Dengan ubat dan exercise, ramai boleh hidup aktif lama.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Saya mulakan Madopar 125mg, setengah biji tiga kali sehari. Take it half an hour before meals, sebab protein dalam makanan boleh halang ubat.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ubat ni ada side effect?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mungkin loya dan pening bila bangun. Kalau dizzy, bangun perlahan-lahan. Ada juga kadang-kadang vivid dreams, mimpi yang pelik.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Solat berdiri macam mana, doktor? Kadang-kadang rasa nak jatuh masa sujud bangun.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kalau rasa tak stabil, solat duduk dulu tak apa. Physio will teach balance exercises. Jumpa lagi dua bulan.

condition: Parkinson's disease with falls and constipation

patient_persona.description: Mrs. Mary Fernandez, 70, female, retired Eurasian nursing tutor in Ipoh; Parkinson's for five years on levodopa; two falls this month, dizzy on standing, constipated. Follow-up. Crisp, precise English with a little Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Mohd Shahrul bin Ismail, Malay man in his 40s, geriatrician at an Ipoh hospital. Gentle, methodical; English-leaning.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mrs. Fernandez, the nurse said you had two falls this month. Can you tell me about them?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Both times getting up from bed at night to go to the loo. Everything went gelap for a moment, then I was on the floor.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Did you hurt yourself? Any head injury?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: A bruise on the hip, lebam je, nothing broken, thank goodness. My neighbour's maid found me the second time.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Your blood pressure lying down is 132 over 80, and standing it drops to 98 over 60. That's orthostatic hypotension, common in Parkinson's.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ah, so it's the Parkinson's causing it, bukan sebab tua.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Partly the Parkinson's, partly the medicines. You're also taking tamsulosin for the bladder, right? That lowers BP further.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, the urologist started it last year for kencing malam.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I'll write to him about changing it. Meanwhile, drink two to two and a half litres a day, and add a little extra salt, unless your heart doctor says no.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I've been drinking less air on purpose, so I won't need the loo at night.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: That makes the dizziness worse. Drink more in the morning and afternoon, less after six. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before standing.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And the constipation, doctor? Sembelit, four days sometimes, very uncomfortable.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Very common in Parkinson's. Take lactulose 15ml at night, more fruit and fibre, and walk daily if you can.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I still jalan in the taman every morning with my tongkat.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Wonderful, keep that up. I'll also ask the occupational therapist to put a bedside commode and night lights at home.

condition: Parkinson's disease, levodopa timing with meals

patient_persona.description: Mariam binti Hassan, 66, female, retired kuih seller in Batu Pahat, Johor; Parkinson's for four years; medicine seems weaker after meals. Refill visit. Warm, slow Johor Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Lee Chun Wai, Malaysian Chinese man in his 30s, family medicine specialist at a Batu Pahat health clinic. Patient, encouraging; English-leaning, speaks colloquial Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mak cik Mariam, datang ambil ubat Madopar, ya? Macam mana sekarang?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ya, doktor. Tapi kadang-kadang ubat macam tak jalan, not working. Lepas makan tengah hari, badan keras, nak jalan pun susah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mak cik makan Madopar tu sebelum makan, atau sama-sama dengan nasi?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Sama-sama, doktor. Anak kata makan ubat mesti after food, nanti perut pedih.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Untuk ubat ni lain sikit. Protein dalam ikan, ayam, susu tu berebut dengan ubat nak masuk otak. Jadi ubat kurang berkesan.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Oh, macam tu. Tengah hari saya memang makan ikan dengan nasi banyak.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Cuba makan Madopar setengah jam before meals. Kalau loya, you can take it with a plain biscuit, biskut kering.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Pagi saya minum susu dengan ubat sekali. Milk pun tak boleh juga?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Susu pun protein. Minum ubat dengan air kosong, susu minum lambat sikit.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Satu lagi, cuba agihkan protein. Makan protein lebih banyak waktu malam, bukan tengah hari.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Nanti saya cakap dengan menantu yang masak. Ubat dos sama ke?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Dos sama dulu, Madopar 125mg tiga kali sehari. Try this new meal timing for two weeks, tengok ada beza tak.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kalau badan masih keras macam tu?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kita tambah dos atau jarakkan waktu. Tulis dalam buku kecil bila badan keras, bila OK, like a diary, bawa masa datang nanti.

condition: Parkinson's disease, missed doses on the ward

patient_persona.description: Goh Teck Chye, 72, male, retired printing shop owner in Butterworth, Penang; Parkinson's for eight years; admitted with pneumonia, missed levodopa doses overnight. Ward round. Weak, soft Penang Mandarin with Hokkien and some Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Lingam a/l Rajoo, Malaysian Indian man in his 30s, medical registrar at a Butterworth hospital. Brisk, respectful; English-leaning, speaks simple Mandarin and Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Goh uncle，早。今天呼吸怎样？还喘吗？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 喘好一点了……但是全身好 stiff，手脚不能动，讲话也很累。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Uncle 的 Sinemet，昨晚几点吃的？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我不知道……护士说我 nil by mouth，因为要照 scan，所以没给我吃。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Okay, that explains the stiffness. Parkinson's ubat tak boleh skip, even one or two doses can make you very stiff.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我自己也跟护士讲了，but 她说要等 doctor order。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 对不起，uncle，这是我们的错。我现在马上 order，Sinemet 立刻给，以后照 schedule，六点、十点、两点、六点。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 如果以后要 nil by mouth，我们会用 NG tube 给药，或者用 patch。不可以没有药。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好……吞东西有时候会 choke，喝 air 会咳。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 这个很重要，可能就是 pneumonia 的原因，aspiration。Speech therapist 今天会来 assess 你的 swallowing。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那我还可以吃粥吗？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 可以，粥比较安全。Air 可能要加一点 thickener，护士会教你。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Antibiotic 继续，co-amoxiclav。你的 oxygen 已经 95 percent，比昨天好。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我太太每天来，她可以帮我 suap 饭吗？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 可以，最好。叫她喂的时候，uncle 要坐直，一口一口慢慢来。下午我再来看你。
